ownership_reason: Only the gold holds the dot product together with the choice between the sine and the cosine formula; hops 1 and 2 compute the norms and their product, hops 3 and 4 pass the pair along. Once the arc cosine of a cosine within a few ulps of 1 has been taken, the lost digits cannot be recovered by any caller, and no change of the inputs (unit vectors, squared norms, another norm product) makes the arc cosine accurate for almost aligned vectors. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the facade's javadoc ('using the dot product for well separated vectors and the cross product for almost aligned vectors ... a good accuracy in all cases, even for vectors very close to each other'); Rotation.getAngle takes the same step for the rotation angle (2 asin of the vector-part norm when |q0| > 0.1, the arc cosine only near a half turn; RotationTest testAxisAngle and testIdentity); Vector3D.crossProduct is preconditioned so that the cross product of almost aligned vectors is accurate (Vector3DTest testCrossProductCancellation).
